title: Indian Professionals Turn to EB-5 Investor Visas as Green Card Waits Stretch Decades
excerpt: With EB-2 wait times exceeding 40 years and H-1B policy uncertainty mounting, a 25-fold surge in Indian EB-5 filings is reshaping the US immigration landscape.
body:
• Indian EB-5 filings surged from 75 in FY2022 to over 3,000 in FY2025, driven by employment-based green card backlogs that stretch 40-60 years for Indian nationals.
  • The July 2026 Visa Bulletin marks EB-2 India and EB-5 Unreserved as "Unavailable" for the rest of FY2026, freezing progress for tens of thousands of skilled workers.
  • A September 30, 2026 grandfathering deadline under the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act is accelerating filings, after which the minimum investment could rise to $920,000-$940,000.
  • Reserved EB-5 categories — Rural, High-Unemployment and Infrastructure — remain current for India, offering a narrowing window for concurrent filing benefits.

A growing number of Indian professionals in the United States are abandoning the traditional H-1B-to-green-card pipeline in favour of the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program, a pathway that until recently was associated almost exclusively with the globally wealthy. The shift is not about wealth migration. It is about professional survival.

The numbers tell the story. Indian EB-5 filings totalled just 75 in fiscal year 2022. By FY2025, that figure had crossed 3,000 — a surge that now makes India the second-largest source of EB-5 petitions globally, accounting for roughly 22% of worldwide receipts, according to IIUSA data and FOIA filings.

A System That Stopped Working

The arithmetic behind the exodus is unforgiving. Over 70% of H-1B visa holders in the United States were born in India, yet federal law caps employment-based green cards for any single country at 7% of the annual total — roughly 9,800 across EB-1, EB-2 and EB-3 combined out of a worldwide pool of about 140,000.

The US State Department's July 2026 Visa Bulletin delivered a stark reminder of the consequences. EB-2 India has been marked "Unavailable" for the remainder of the fiscal year after all visa numbers were exhausted. The EB-3 queue for India sits at January 1, 2014 — meaning USCIS is processing applications filed more than 12 years ago. EB-5 Unreserved is similarly frozen for India.

"If demand from Indian nationals continues at this pace, we could see EB-5 backlogs form within reserved categories — just like they did in EB-2."

— Charlie Oppenheim, former Chief of the Visa Office, US Department of State

"EB-2 India has been marked "Unavailable" for the remainder of the fiscal year after all visa numbers were exhausted."

"EB-2 India has been marked "Unavailable" for the remainder of the fiscal year after all visa numbers were exhausted."

For a mid-career engineer or finance professional who has spent a decade in the US, bought a home, enrolled children in school and built a career, the green card timeline under the employment-based system is measured not in years but in working lifetimes. At current rates, professionals filing EB-2 petitions today will not receive a green card before retirement.

Why EB-5, Why Now

The EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 changed the calculus. For the first time, it allowed applicants already in the US to file for adjustment of status concurrently with their EB-5 petition, receiving work authorisation and travel permission while their case is pending. A US-based professional could initiate an independent immigration pathway without quitting a job, losing status or leaving the country.

The minimum investment stands at $800,000 for projects in Targeted Employment Areas, with the standard amount at $1,050,000. Mid-career H-1B holders are converting stock options, savings and retirement funds into the required capital. The investment is returned at the end of the loan term, typically within three to five years.

Rural EB-5 projects currently process I-526E petitions in four to nine months, compared to 18 to 24 months for high-unemployment area projects, according to StudentEB5's June 2026 investor guide. Both reserved categories — Rural, High-Unemployment and Infrastructure — remain current for India even as the Unreserved lane has frozen.

The Ticking Clock

A grandfathering provision tied to the 2022 reform carries a September 30, 2026 deadline. Applicants who file before that date can lock in the existing $800,000 investment threshold and preserve access to legacy Regional Center programme benefits. After that date, an inflation adjustment is expected to push the minimum TEA investment to between $920,000 and $940,000 in 2027.

The Trump administration's approach to H-1B has compounded the urgency. Policy unpredictability, layoffs across technology and professional services, and a 60-day grace period following job loss have exposed how precarious employer-sponsored status can be. The H-4 EAD rollback of 540 days and weighted H-1B selection have further eroded confidence in the temporary-visa pipeline.

What This Means for the Diaspora

For the roughly five-million-strong Indian-American community — and the larger cohort on temporary visas hoping to put down permanent roots — the EB-5 pivot is both a financial calculation and an existential one. The question a mid-career H-1B holder is asking, as described in an Economic Times commentary, is straightforward: is an $800,000 investment with work authorisation in hand a better outcome than remaining on employer-sponsored status for an indeterminate number of additional decades?

For a growing number, the answer is yes. Documentation remains a practical hurdle — applicants must navigate Reserve Bank of India rules, the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, TDS compliance and FEMA regulations to move funds abroad.

Looking Ahead

The October 1 reset, when fiscal year 2027 begins and fresh visa numbers are allocated, will reopen EB-2 and EB-5 Unreserved for India. But "reopen" is not the same as "advance." Immigration attorneys are already warning that reserved EB-5 categories could face their own retrogression if Indian petition volumes continue climbing.

The H-1B bottleneck was always going to push Indian professionals toward alternatives. The combination of structural backlog, policy uncertainty and a reformed EB-5 programme has accelerated that timeline. The window — at the current investment threshold — closes on September 30.
